..
As of 325 AM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Well above normal temperatures with mostly dry 
conditions are expected through Friday. Record breaking highs are 
possible Wednesday. 

High pressure is building into the region from the SW early this 
morning. A surface low and cold front are noted across MI. Mainly 
clear skies and light winds are allowing for areas of ground fog 
across the area. A more widespread area of fog may develop across 
the Piedmont/I-95 corridor prior to sunrise. 

Ridging will continue to spread NE from the Gulf Coast today, 
resulting in mostly clear skies and well above normal temperatures 
this afternoon. High temps climb into the low and mid 80s inland and 
upper 70s to low 80s near the coast. Lows tonight will be in the low 
to mid 60s. Heights build aloft on Wednesday with record breaking 
high temps looking increasingly likely. Blended guidance shows high 
temps in the upper 80s to around 90 degrees. However, all the 
statistical guidance is a degree or two warmer with widespread low 
90s for inland locations. Went a bit above the blended guidance but 
not as high as the MOS would suggest for now. Regardless, this 
results in highs above the record temps for the day Wednesday. See 
the climate section below for specific values. Records could be 
broken by several degrees at the main climate sites. A cold front 
will approach the region from the N Wednesday night and is forecast 
to cross most of the local area on Thursday. 00z guidance shows the 
front making it much through most if not all of the area before 
stalling. This will allow for a break in the heat for the majority 
of the CWA on Thursday with highs ranging from near 70 degrees 
across the northern counties, mid to upper 70s along and south of I-
64, and low to even mid 80s near and south of the VA/NC border. 
Clouds will thicken from N to S Thursday as the front drops south. 
In addition, some weak isentropic lift north of the front could 
result in generally light rain across the northern third of the area 
Thursday. QPF is on the order of a few hundredths of an inch. A deep 
upper trough is forecast to dig across the Great Lakes Thursday 
night into Friday with a strengthening surface low over the Ohio 
Valley. Southerly flow ahead of this feature will allow the front to 
lift back northward as a warm front Friday morning. High temps 
rebound into the upper 70s to low 80s N with mid and upper 80s S. It 
will become breezy out of the SW by Friday afternoon. Some showers 
and thunder are also possible, primarily across NE portions of the 
area Friday afternoon. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Much cooler temperatures arrive this weekend. Frost 
is possible across portions of the area. 

Rapidly deepening low pressure will translate NE into New England on 
Friday with a strong cold front extending back to the southwest. 
This front will cross the local area Friday evening into early 
Saturday with significant cold advection moving into the region. 
Some additional precip is possible along and ahead of the frontal 
passage, mainly over the eastern half of the area before midnight. 
QPF does not look nearly as impressive as a front of this strength 
would suggest. Strong (1035mb+) high pressure builds into the region 
behind the front with upper troughing remaining over the eastern 
CONUS, resulting in well below normal temperatures this weekend. 
Afternoon highs likely struggle to get out of the 50s across the 
northern half of the CWA despite mostly sunny skies. Low 60s are 
forecast for the southern half of the area. It will also be quite 
breezy on Saturday with gusts 25-30mph, and especially near the 
coast where winds could gust 30-35mph. Overnight low temps tumble 
into the mid to upper 30s in the Piedmont with low to mid 40s for 
the remainder of the area Saturday night. Upper 30s and low 40s are 
forecast Sunday night into Monday. Some frost is possible in the 
Piedmont with this airmass.
